description:
Pinpointed the EXACT root cause of the frontmatter corruption previously logged in err-20260825T081039-APAWBB and err-20260826T081314-NBGENM, which both guessed at the mechanism without isolating it, and NBGENM explicitly (and incorrectly) concluded the current salience-score.py version 'does not add new orphaned lines going forward.' It does, every single night, on every file. Root cause, confirmed by direct reproduction in isolation: systems/dream-cycle/salience-score.py's main() finds the frontmatter boundary via `end = content.find("
---", 3)` and slices `fm_section = content[3:end]`, which EXCLUDES the newline immediately preceding the closing `---` delimiter. Since the salience: block is always the last block in the frontmatter (written that way by both step-01's enrichment and the script's own prior appends), its final line never has a trailing '
' inside fm_section. update_salience_block()'s removal regex `r"
salience:\s*
(?:[ 	]+[^
]*
)*"` requires every retained line in that repeating group to END with '
' -- so it strips 'salience:
' plus every line EXCEPT the last one, and the last line (whatever it is: 'score: 0' on a brand-new block, or 'promoted: true' on a previously-promoted one) is left stranded immediately after whatever field preceded 'salience:' (typically related_people). A fresh, clean salience: block is then appended, and the stranding repeats the next night on the NEW last line. This is why the corpus shows one new duplicate orphaned line per file per night: it is not random or file-specific, it fires deterministically on every file salience-score.py touches, every run. Reproduced live this cycle on a file I had just written completely clean minutes earlier (memory/episodic/dream-summary-2026-08-26.md, archived fresh in this cycle's own step-01): its single-line 'salience:
  score: 0' block became 'related_people: []
  score: 0
salience:
  score: 10
  last-promoted-check: 2026-08-28' after this cycle's step-02 run -- corruption appearing within the same session that wrote the clean version, proving it is an active, currently-firing bug, not frozen legacy damage. Secondary consequence also newly confirmed: parse_frontmatter()'s promoted-detection regex `re.search(r"^\s*promoted:\s*(true|false)", fm_text, re.MULTILINE)` returns the FIRST match top-to-bottom, not the authoritative last one. Three files promoted in the prior (2026-08-27) cycle -- co-sell-pipeline-2026-08-24-001532.md, dream-summary-2026-08-25.md, revenue-tracker-2026-08-24-002000.md -- already carried a stray unindented-looking 'promoted: false' line under related_people from an EARLIER stranding event, positioned before their salience block's legitimate 'promoted: true'. This cycle's scoring run matched the earlier 'false' first, treated them as not-yet-promoted, and silently dropped 'promoted: true' from their freshly-written salience block (while stranding yet another orphaned line). Had this cycle's step-03 candidate-detection relied on only the rightmost salience: block (the method prior cycles documented as their workaround), it would have wrongly re-flagged these 3 already-promoted entries as fresh candidates and re-appended duplicate evidence to their semantic targets. Worked around this cycle by scanning the ENTIRE frontmatter text for any 'promoted: true' occurrence (not just the last salience block) before treating an entry as a genuine new candidate -- confirmed this correctly excluded all 4 previously-promoted files from the 08-25/26/27 cycles and left exactly 1 genuine new candidate (this cycle's own fresh archive).
correction: No corpus-wide repair or script edit attempted -- systems/ is Rigby-gated per SYSTEM.md's Pre-Write Gate, consistent with how APAWBB and NBGENM were handled. For this cycle's own step-03 write (setting salience.promoted:true on the single new candidate), will hand-edit the file's salience: block directly with an exact string replace rather than relying on the buggy script or an ad-hoc regex, to avoid contributing a fresh instance of this exact corruption.
systemic_fix:
The fix is now precisely scoped, not a guess: in systems/dream-cycle/salience-score.py, either (a) append the frontmatter's own trailing newline back before slicing (`fm_section = content[3:end] + '
'`, adjusting `rest` to compensate) so the last line of any block always ends in '
' before the removal regex runs, or (b) change the removal regex's trailing element to `[ 	]+[^
]*
?` (optional trailing newline) so it can consume a final line lacking one. Also fix parse_frontmatter()'s promoted-detection to use `list(re.finditer(...))[-1]` (last match) instead of `re.search()` (first match), so a stray earlier orphan can never shadow the authoritative current value. Finally, run a ONE-TIME corpus repair (out of nightly scope, a capability-level fix for Rigby) that, for every episodic file, collects all 'promoted:'/'last-promoted-check:'/'score:' lines regardless of position, keeps only the correct current values, and rewrites a single well-formed trailing salience: block -- this closes out both APAWBB and NBGENM as well as this entry in one pass.
